evidence.s1_requirements: BehaviourTree.snapshot() returns {version, root} plain object (step1.patch BehaviourTree.ts +2010-2015); BehaviourTreeSnapshot and NodeSnapshot exported from src/index.ts; restore() validates then applies (BehaviourTree.ts:148-179). Snapshot keeps state of every node and children (Composite/Decorator getSnapshot), repeat/retry current+target counts (Repeat.ts:101-107, Retry), lotto selectedChildIndex (Lotto.ts:75-80), wait totalDuration/waitedDuration (Wait.ts:112-127). Restored wait only waits the remaining time in both modes (Wait.ts:155 sets initialUpdateTime = now - waited; getDeltaTime accumulates waitedDuration); tests spec:399-520. Finished tree restores finished and re-picks randomness (spec:207-225, 335-354, 557). README documents API with a correct example.
evidence.s1_correctness: Equivalence spec restores a fresh tree at each of 90 steps for three definitions covering sequence/selector/repeat/retry/lotto/wait/parallel/race/all/flip/succeed/fail, while/until guards, entry/step/exit callbacks, under both the clock and getDeltaTime, and asserts identical node states, results, agent call log, random-sequence position and snapshot round trip (BehaviourTreeSnapshotEquivalence.spec.ts:154-235). Action keeps settled promise outcomes as strings, which preserves the exact error messages (Action.ts:186-229). Restore into the same tree ignores old in-flight promises (updatePromise identity, spec:807-833). Infinite waited time is clamped for JSON (Wait.ts:125).
evidence.s2_validation: Definition id is a two-seed 53-bit hash of a canonicalised JSON definition (sorted keys, empty args and false succeedOnAbort dropped, roots sorted by id) (step2.patch BehaviourTreeSnapshotUtilities.ts +521-591). Mismatch throws 'error restoring tree: snapshot does not match the tree's definition' (BehaviourTree.ts:164-166). Tests: MDSL vs JSON equivalence including reordering and explicit defaults (spec:1030-1111); different definitions with same node names/types rejected and tree unchanged (spec:998-1019); null/string/number/array/field-less object rejected (spec:1340-1366). Pending promise saved as READY (Action.ts:188-192) and documented in README 'Promise-based actions' with the entry-callback consequence; tests spec:705-805.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug 1 fixed at its cause: prepareRestore assigns _state directly instead of setState (step3.patch Node.ts:306-312); the agent's own step 1 test that asserted the old behaviour was changed to assert no calls during restore and normal reporting on the next step (step3.patch:297-326). Bug 2: no code change, since snapshots were already freshly built and restore copies values. A regression suite was added for repeat/retry/lotto/wait/action (step3.patch:213-288), but only with getDeltaTime: on a real clock, a snapshot taken after restore includes elapsed ms and is untested. The Version History does not say the second report needed no fix. The README removed the now-obsolete note about onNodeStateChange errors; no unrelated changes.
evidence.design: Each node class owns getSnapshot/prepareRestore with a validate-then-apply closure pattern that guarantees no partial restore (Node.ts:284-335, Composite, Decorator, Lotto, Repeat, Retry, Action, Wait). Shared helpers live in BehaviourTreeSnapshotUtilities.ts and the snapshot types in BehaviourTreeSnapshot.ts, following the repo's file naming and doc-comment style. Weaknesses: NodeSnapshot is one flat type with many optional per-node fields rather than per-node types; the 'possible picked value' plausibility checks add code beyond the ask; the Action promise identity change alters baseline behaviour (justified for restoring into the same tree).
evidence.tests: Two new mocha/chai/sinon specs in test/ (BehaviourTreeSnapshot.spec.ts ~1400 lines, BehaviourTreeSnapshotEquivalence.spec.ts) plus an Action.spec.ts test for the promise-identity fix. They cover every requirement and edge case (random counts and durations, both time modes, finished trees, lotto, pending/settled/rejected promises, invalid input, definition mismatch, independence, no onNodeStateChange). They use fake timers. No existing test was removed or weakened.
evidence.docs: README: feature bullet, snapshot()/restore() API entries, a 'Saving and Restoring a Tree' section with a correct fs-based example, what is and isn't saved, restore behaviour, and the pending-promise limitation (step1/2/3 README diffs). Version History rows for 4.4.0 (feature plus the action promise fix) and 4.4.1 (onNodeStateChange fix); package.json and package-lock bumped accordingly.
evidence.process: 19 commits, each focused with conventional, descriptive messages (feat/fix/test/docs/build), and dist regeneration in separate build commits (the repo tracks dist). No new dependencies; package-lock changes are only the version field. One baseline-adjacent fix (c640a6d, ignoring stale action promises) is required for correct restore into the same tree and is tested and noted in the Version History.

strengths: Each node type saves and restores its own state, and restore validates everything before it changes anything, so a rejected restore cannot leave the tree half-changed
An equivalence test restores a new tree at every step of runs that use every node type and source of randomness, in both time modes, and checks it behaves exactly like the original
MDSL and equivalent JSON produce the same definition id via a canonical form, with thorough tests of acceptance, rejection with the stated message, and invalid input
issues: Step 3 report 2 got only tests, no code change, which is correct since nothing was shared between snapshot and tree; but the independence suite uses only getDeltaTime, so on a real clock a snapshot taken after restore() can differ by elapsed ms, and the Version History doesn't say no fix was needed
NodeSnapshot is one flat type with many optional per-node fields instead of a type per node, which makes the exported type loose
Extra plausibility checks on restore and the Action promise-identity change go a little beyond what was asked (both are tested and justified)
review.verdict: A careful, well-tested implementation that meets every requirement across the three steps, with per-node state ownership, validation that never leaves a tree half-restored, and an exhaustive equivalence test in both time modes. The remaining gaps are minor: report 2 is backed only by delta-time tests, and the node snapshot type is loose.
